matchedFilings.description: ORDER OF CONSOLIDATION. There are currently nine actions pending before the undersigned related to Defendant's alleged data breach incident on May 23, 2026: 26-CV-833; 26-CV-835; 26-CV-847; 26-CV-848; 26-CV-850; 26-CV-868; 26-CV-893; 26-CV-918; and 26-CV-947. In Case No. 26-CV-835, Plaintiff filed a motion for consolidation, indicating that there is a significant overlap among the factual issues and claims in each of these actions. Defendant has responded to the motion, expressing no objection to consolidation of these actions for pretrial purposes. Accordingly, as there are "common question[s] of law and fact" in all of these cases, see Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a), and absent objection, the cases bearing the following docket numbers are hereby consolidated with this action for pretrial purposes only: 26-CV-833; 26-CV-835; 26-CV-847; 26-CV-848; 26-CV-850; 26-CV-868; 26-CV-893; 26-CV-918; and 26-CV-947.The lead case shall be 26-CV-833, as it is the first-filed action. Motions for appointment of interim class counsel shall be filed in the Lead Case by any interested Plaintiffs' counsel by August 20, 2026. Defendant's deadline to answer or otherwise respond to the operative complaint in the Lead Case (and each independent action) is hereby suspended, in anticipation of a consolidated amended class action complaint being filed in the Lead Case after appointment of interim class counsel. The Court also suspends the parties' deadline to file a Rule 26(f) report in all of the actions, including the Lead Case, and will reset this deadline following the appointment of interim class counsel. Signed by Judge Sarala V. Nagala on 7/23/2026.(sd) (Entered: 07/23/2026)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER OF CONSOLIDATION. There are currently nine actions pending before the undersigned related to Defendant's alleged data breach incident on May 23, 2026: 26-CV-833; 26-CV-835; 26-CV-847; 26-CV-848; 26-CV-850; 26-CV-868; 26-CV-893; 26-CV-918; and 26-CV-947. In Case No. 26-CV-835, Plaintiff filed a motion for consolidation, indicating that there is a significant overlap among the factual issues and claims in each of these actions. Defendant has responded to the motion, expressing no objection to consolidation of these actions for pretrial purposes. Accordingly, as there are "common question[s] of law and fact" in all of these cases, see Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a), and absent objection, the cases bearing the following docket numbers are hereby consolidated with this action for pretrial purposes only: 26-CV-833; 26-CV-835; 26-CV-847; 26-CV-848; 26-CV-850; 26-CV-868; 26-CV-893; 26-CV-918; and 26-CV-947.The lead case shall be 26-CV-833, as it is the first-filed action. Motions for appointment of interim class counsel shall be filed in the Lead Case by any interested Plaintiffs' counsel by August 20, 2026. Defendant's deadline to answer or otherwise respond to the operative complaint in the Lead Case (and each independent action) is hereby suspended, in anticipation of a consolidated amended class action complaint being filed in the Lead Case after appointment of interim class counsel. The Court also suspends the parties' deadline to file a Rule 26(f) report in all of the actions, including the Lead Case, and will reset this deadline following the appointment of interim class counsel. Signed by Judge Sarala V. Nagala on 7/23/2026.(sd) (Entered: 07/23/2026)

US Tiger Securities Inc., No. 1:26-cv-04299, filed on May 22, 2026, (the "Related Cases") are consolidated purs uant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings , and conserve the resources of the parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the docket number of the first-filed Tillberry case, No. 1:26-cv-04223, presently before this Court and filed in this District , and any future related actions arising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court, under the low-numbered case with the caption In re US Tiger Securities Inc. Data Breach Litigat ion; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Melissa G. Meyer of Levi & Korsinsky, LLP and Courtney Maccarone of Kopelowitz Ostrow, P.A. are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Rel ated Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of the Order; and IT IS SO ORDERED. All filings in the member cases shall be in the lead case, 26-CV-4223. For administrative pur poses, the Clerk of Court is directed to close the two other later-filed actions listed above. matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE ACTIONS AND APPOINT INTERIM CO-LEAD CLASS COUNSEL granting (9) Motion to Consolidate Cases 26-cv-01362 (as Lead Case) with 26-cv-01655 in case 1:26-cv-01362-LAK. The Court hereby GRANTS the Motion and hereby ORDERS as follows : The related actions pending in this District, listed below, are consolidated for all purposes, including pretrial proceedings, trial, and appeal, pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a) (hereafter, the "Consolidated Actions"): Ace Cam, Inc. v. Runway AI, Inc., Case No. 1 :26-cv-01362-LAK. Businessing LLC v. v. Runway AL Inc., Case No. 1:26-cv-01655-LAK. The Consolidated Actions, as well as any other actions subsequently consolidated with them, shall be coordinated to the extent practicable with one another under one docket for purposes of discovery and pretrial proceedings to promote efficiency in managing and litigating the cases. The files of the Consolidated Actions shall be maintained under the Master File Case No. 26-cv-01362-LAK, the docket number assigned to the first-filed case. This order shall apply to all related actions subsequently filed in or transferred to this District that arise out of the same or similar operative facts as the Consolidated Actions. Any subsequently filed actions that are filed in, or transferred to, this Court will be, absent objection, deemed related and consolidated under the Master Docket, Case. No. 26-cv-01362- LAK, within 10 calendar days following the filing or transfer of that action. If any party objects to such consolidation or otherwise wishes to seek alternative relief, they must do so before the expiration of that period. The Court appoints Tom Kherkher of Ellzey Kherkher Sanford Montgomery LLP and Gary Klinger of Milberg, PLLC, as Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plainitffs pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g). All deadlines in the Consolidated Cases are vacated; and Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within forty-five (45) days of the Order. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Lewis A. Kaplan on 3/27/26) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:26-cv-01362-LAK, 1:26-cv-01655-LAK (yv) (Entered: 03/27/2026)

matchedFilings.description: Minute Entry for proceeding held before Judge Cathy Seibel: Status Conference held on 2/26/2026. Counsel(s) for Plaintiff Giannasca (25 CV 6440) - Thomas Burt, Esq., Julian Diamond, Esq., and Spencer Migotsky, Esq. are present. Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Gelbspan et al (25 CV 10397) - Blake Yagman, Esq. appears telephonically. Counsel(s) for Plaintiff(s) Donovan et al (25 CV 10571) - Daniel Silverman, Esq. and Emily Marcus, Esq. are present. Counsel for Plaintiff Redner's Market, Inc. (25 CV 10633) - Candice Enders, Esq. is present. Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Lee et al (26 CV 329) - Christopher Micheletti, Esq. is present. Counsel(s) for Plaintiff(s) Davis (26 CV 405) and Petretti (26 CV 1486) - Matthew Weiler, Esq. and David Burnett, Esq. are present. Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Fargo Shopping Center LLC et al (26 CV 1283) - Joshua Rissman, Esq. and Miles Greaves, Esq. are present. Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Arbit et al (26 CV 1455) - Andrew Szot, Esq. is present. Plaintiff's counsel Thomas Burt, Esq. also speaking on behalf of Plaintiff Emporium Food Store LLC (25 CV 10698). Counsel(s) for Defendant(s) PepsiCo, Inc. and PepsiCo Beverage Sales, LLC, Jay Srinivasan, Esq. and Laura O'Boyle, Esq., are present. Counsel for Defendant Walmart, Inc., Lawrence Buterman, Esq., is present. Law Clerk Ryan Miller is present. Plaintiffs' brief(s) (joint or contested) regarding leadership for direct purchaser Plaintiffs to be submitted by March 6, 2026. Reply briefs, if any, to be submitted by March 13, 2026. Also, Plaintiffs' brief(s) (joint or contested) regarding leadership for indirect purchasers to be submitted by March 6, 2026 with replies (if any) by March 13, 2026. Consolidated Class Action Complaint(s) to be filed forty-five (45) days after leadership decided. Pre-Motion letter(s) to be submitted thirty (30) days after Complaint(s) filed. Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaints (for direct retailer purchasers, direct end user purchasers, and indirect purchasers) to be submitted thirty (30) days after pre-motion letters. Motion(s) to Dismiss to be submitted sixty (60) days after Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaints submitted. Opposition to Motion to Dismiss to be submitted forty-five (45) days after motion, and reply due thirty (30) days after opposition. The Court hereby GRANTS the motion to consolidate these cases for pre-trial purposes. The Court will issue a written Order. The Court also DENIES without prejudice Plaintiff's Motion (Doc # 5) in the Gelbspan case (25 CV 10397). See transcript. (Court Reporter Angela O'Donnell) Associated Cases: 7:25-cv-06440-CS et al.(wc)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR CONSOLIDATION AND APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL AND AN EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE granting (20) Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:25-cv-07109-AT; granting (22) Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:25-cv-07183-AT; granting (21) Letter Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:26-cv-00702-AT. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1.Butler-Adams v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. No. 1:25-cv-7109; Miamen v.Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7183; Godinez v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7280; Moran v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7241; Guanzon v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7240; and Winkler v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:26-cv-00702 (the "Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the docket number of the first-filed Butler-Adams action, No. 1:25-cv-7109, presently before this Court and filed in this District, and any future related actions arising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court, under the low-numbered case with the caption In re Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. Data Breach Litigation; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Daniel Srourian of Srourian Law Firm, P.C. and Hunter Bryson of Bryson, Harris, Suciu & DeMay, PLLC are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs and Israel David of Israel David LLC, Amber Schubert of Schubert Jonckheer & Kolbe LLP, Mark Reich of Levi & Korsinksky, LLP, and Steven Nathan of Hausfeld, LLP are hereby appointed as members of an Executive Committee for Plaintiffs, with Steven Nathan serving as Chairperson of the Executive Committee; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of the Order; and 7.In accordance with the Court's January 12, 2026 Order, Defendant shall respond tothe Consolidated Class Action Complaint within forty-five (45) days after the Consolidated Class Action Complaint is filed, and the parties shall file a joint letter and proposed case management plan within sixty (60) days after the Consolidated Class Action Complaint is filed; By June 11, 2026, Plaintiffs shall file their consolidated class action complaint. The Clerk of Court is respectfully directed to consolidate these matters under the caption In re: Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. Data Breach Litigation, case number 25 Civ. 7109. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Analisa Torres on 5/12/2026) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-07109-AT et al. (vfr) (Entered: 05/12/2026)

At that conference, the Court will discuss the options for consolidation of these three actions for purposes of the Kalshi Defendants' pending and anticipated motions to compel arbitration, and for purposes of future proceedings. It is further ORDERED that the parties shall, prior to the February, 5, 2026 conference, file a Proposed Stipulation to Consolidate Actions and Set Scheduling Deadlines, setting forth protocols for docketing in this matter, as well as a schedule for motions for the appointment of a lead plaintiff and interim lead counsel pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g)(3), for the filing of a consolidated amended class action complaint, and for the filing of the Kalshi Defendants' motion to compel arbitration. Any remaining legal issues can be addressed at the conference. Counsel are directed to review and comply with the Court's Individual Rules of Practice in Civil Cases, available at JLR Rochon Individual Rules of Practice in Civil Cases - June 23, 2025.pdf. (And as further set forth herein.) SO ORDERED. (Status Conference set for 2/5/2026 at 11:30 AM in Courtroom 20B, 500 Pearl Street, New York, NY 10007 before Judge Jennifer L. Rochon.) matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE ACTIONS AND APPOINT INTERIM CO-LEAD CLASS COUNSEL 10 Motion to Consolidate Cases 26cv00021 (as Lead Case) with 26cv00074, 26cv00077. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1. Handy v. Rockrose Dev elopment L.L.C., No. 1:26-cv-00021-CM ("Handy") filed on January 2, 2026; Vauvelle v. Rockrose Development, L.L.C., No. l:26-cv-00074 ("Vauvelle") filed on January 6, 2026; and Martinez v. Rockrose Development, LLC, No. 1:26-cv-00 077-MMG ("Martinez" ) filed on January 6, 2026 (collectively the " Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the c aption In re Rockrose Data Breach Litigation with the docket number of the first-filed Handy action, No. 1 :26-cv-00021-CM, presently before this Court and filed in this District; and any future related actions arising from the same data breach as th e Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court shall be consolidated into this same action; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Adam M. Harris of Israel David LLC, Kevin Laukaitis of Laukaitis Law LL C, and Gerald D. Wells, III of Lynch Carpenter, LLP are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of entry of this Order; and 7. Defendant shall file an answer or respond to the Consolidated Class Action Complaint within forty-five (45) days of service thereof. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Colleen McMahon on 03/19/2026) (ar)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE ACTIONS AND APPOINT INTERIM CO-LEAD CLASS COUNSEL 10 Motion to Consolidate Cases 26cv00021 (as Lead Case) with 26cv00074, 26cv00077. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1. H andy v. Rockrose Development L.L.C., No. 1:26-cv-00021-CM ("Handy") filed on January 2, 2026; Vauvelle v. Rockrose Development, L.L.C., No. l:26-cv-00074 ("Vauvelle") filed on January 6, 2026; and Martinez v. Rockrose D evelopment, LLC, No. 1:26-cv-00077-MMG ("Martinez" ) filed on January 6, 2026 (collectively the " Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is a ppropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties, their coun sel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the caption In re Rockrose Data Breach Litigation with the docket number of the first-filed Handy action, No. 1 :26-cv-00021-CM, presently before t his Court and filed in this District; and any future related actions arising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court shall be consolidated into this same action; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Adam M. Harris of Israel David LLC, Kevin Laukaitis of Laukaitis Law LLC, and Gerald D. Wells, III of Lynch Carpenter, LLP are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of entry of this Order; and 7. Defendant shall file an answer or respond to the Consolidated Class Action Complaint within forty-five (45) days of service thereof. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Colleen McMahon on 3/19/2026) (ar)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER: On November 24, 2025, Plaintiff Daniel Salabaj filed a class action complaint in 25-CV-9776 against Stubhub Holdings, Inc (Stubhub), alleging securities fraud. On December 9, 2025, Plaintiff Kevin Junco filed a shareholder derivative complaint against StubHub in 25-CV-10208. As of this Order, no motion for consolidation has been filed, but 25-CV-10208 has been accepted by the Court as related to 25-CV-9776, and the cases appear to involve common questions of law and fact. In light of that, the parties in both cases are directed to confer and, no later than December 22, 2025, file a joint letter advising the Court whether and to what extent the two cases should be consolidated or coordinated. Unless and until the Court orders otherwise, the motion deadlines and the hearing date for appointment of a lead plaintiff in 25-CV-9776 (see Docket Nos. 7, 18) remain in effect. If any party believes that the dates, deadlines, or procedures should be modified, it shall file a letter motion to that effect by December 22, 2025. It is further ORDERED that the named plaintiffs shall promptly serve a copy of this Order on each of the defendants and file proof of service on the docket. SO ORDERED. (Motions due by 12/22/2025.) (Signed by Judge Jesse M. Furman on 12/15/2025) (jca) (Entered: 12/15/2025)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR CONSOLIDATION AND APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL granting (8 in 1:25-cv-10040-ER) Letter Motion to Consolidate Cases. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1. Maggio v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-100 40 filed on December 3, 2025, Rifai v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-10119 filed on December 5, 2025, and Veloz v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-10198 filed on December 10, 2025 (the "Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ . P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arises from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the docket number of the first-filed Maggio action, No. 1:25-cv-10040, presently before this Court and filed in this District, and any future relat ed actions arising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court, under the low-numbered case with the caption: In re Byzfunder NY LLC Data Breach Litigation; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rul e of Civil Procedure 23(g), Daniel Srourian of Srourian Law Firm, P.C., Mariya Weekes of Milberg, PLLC, and Hunter Bryson of Bryson Harris Suciu & DeMay PLLC are hereby appointed Interim Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of the Order. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Edgardo Ramos on 1/15/2026) (jca)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR CONSOLIDATION AND APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL granting 8 Letter Motion to Consolidate Cases. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1. Maggio v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-10040 filed on Decem ber 3, 2025, Rifai v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-10119 filed on December 5, 2025, and Veloz v. Byzfunder NY LLC, No. 1:25-cv-10198 filed on December 10, 2025 (the "Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arises from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of t he parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the docket number of the first-filed Maggio action, No. 1:25-cv-10040, presently before this Court and filed in this District, and any future related actions a rising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court, under the low-numbered case with the caption: In re Byzfunder NY LLC Data Breach Litigation; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Daniel Srourian of Srourian Law Firm, P.C., Mariya Weekes of Milberg, PLLC, and Hunter Bryson of Bryson Harris Suciu & DeMay PLLC are hereby appointed Interim Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of the Order. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Edgardo Ramos on 1/15/2026) (jca)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE ACTIONS AND APPOINT INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL AND AN EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE granting (10) Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:25-cv-09748-LJL. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1. Kelechian v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-09748; Stack v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-09773; Lewis v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-09824; Dunham v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-09898; Thomas v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-09969; Clarke v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 7:25-cv-09994; and Phillips v. SitusAmc Holdings Corporation, No. 1:25-cv-010043 (the Related Cases) are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolid ation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolidation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties , their counsel and the judiciary; as further set forth in this Order. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Mariya Weekes of Milberg, PLLC, and Gregory Haroutunian of Emery Reddy, PC, are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counse l for Plaintiffs, and Courtney Maccarone of Kopelowitz Ostrow, P.A., Jessica Wilkes of Federman Sherwood, Andrew Fuller of Cotchett Pitre & McCarthy, LLP, Leanna A. Loginov of Shamis & Gentile, and Leigh S. Montgomery of Ellzey Kherkher Sanford Montg omery, LLP are hereby appointed as members of an Executive Committee for Plaintiffs; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint within thirty (30) days of the Order. At the s ame time the amended complaint is filed, counsel shall file a proposed order setting forth the functions of lead counsel and of each member of the executive committee. See Manual for Complex Litigation 10.222 (2004). 7. The Clerk of Court is di rected to consolidate all cases listed above under case number 25-cv-9748. Counsel are directed to make filings only under case number 25-cv-9748. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Lewis J. Liman on 12/19/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-09748-LJL et al. (ks)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER: On November 24, 2025, Plaintiff Daniel Salabaj filed a class action complaint in 25-CV-9776 against Stubhub Holdings, Inc (Stubhub), alleging securities fraud. On December 9, 2025, Plaintiff Kevin Junco filed a shareholder derivative complaint against StubHub in 25-CV-10208. As of this Order, no motion for consolidation has been filed, but 25-CV-10208 has been accepted by the Court as related to 25-CV-9776, and the cases appear to involve common questions of law and fact. In light of that, the parties in both cases are directed to confer and, no later than December 22, 2025, file a joint letter advising the Court whether and to what extent the two cases should be consolidated or coordinated. Unless and until the Court orders otherwise, the motion deadlines and the hearing date for appointment of a lead plaintiff in 25-CV-9776 (see Docket Nos. 7, 18) remain in effect. If any party believes that the dates, deadlines, or procedures should be modified, it shall file a letter motion to that effect by December 22, 2025. It is further ORDERED that the named plaintiffs shall promptly serve a copy of this Order on each of the defendants and file proof of service on the docket. SO ORDERED. (Motions due by 12/22/2025.) (Signed by Judge Jesse M. Furman on 12/15/2025) (jca) (Entered: 12/15/2025)

DOCKET TEXT ORDER. In 1 Class Action Complaint, Plaintiff invokes this court's diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d) but fails adequately to allege Defendant's citizenship. Plaintiff alleges that Defendant "is a private company organized and existing under the laws of Cyprus, with a place of business in Dallas, Texas." Dkt. No. 1 ¶ 7. But if Defendant is a corporation, Plaintiff must allege not only each State (or foreign nation) in which the Defendant is incorporated, but also the State or foreign nation where the Defendant "has its principal place of business." 28 U.S.C. § 1332(c)(1) (emphasis added). A corporation's principal place of business "should normally be the place where the corporation maintains its headquartersprovided that the headquarters is the actual center of direction, control, and coordination, i.e., the 'nerve center,' and not simply an office where the corporation holds its board meetings (for example, attended by directors and officers who have traveled there for the occasion)." Hertz Corp. v. Friend, 559 U.S. 77, 93 (2010). If Defendant is an LLC or some other sort of unincorporated entity or association, Plaintiff must identify all of the entity's members and allege each member's citizenship, for it is well settled that "any non-corporate artificial entity" takes on "the citizenship of all [its] members." Conagra Foods, Inc. v. Americold Logistics, LLC, 776 F.3d 1175, 1180 (10th Cir. 2015) (quoting Carden v. Arkoma Assocs., 494 U.S. 185, 195 (1990)); see also Siloam Springs Hotel, L.L.C. v. Century Sur. Co., 781 F.3d 1233, 123738 (10th Cir. 2015). If any of the unincorporated entity's members is itself an LLC or other unincorporated entity, then Plaintiff must also identify all members of that constituent entity and allege the citizenship of each of those members, "tracing through however many layers necessary to reach either a corporation or a natural person." Choice Hospice, Inc. v. Axxess Tech. Sols., Inc., 125 F.4th 1000, 1009 (10th Cir. 2025) (cleaned up). No later than Monday, March 30, 2026, Plaintiff shall file an amended complaint that alleges whether Defendant is a corporation, an LLC, or some other sort of noncorporate entity and then adequately alleges Defendant's citizenship for purposes of diversity jurisdiction. See 28 U.S.C. § 1653. If the amended complaint fails adequately to allege diversity between the parties, this action will be dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction. SO ORDERED. Signed by Judge Howard C. Nielson, Jr., on 3/8/2026. (jad) (Entered: 03/08/2026)

matchedFilings.description: TEXT ORDER entered by Judge Michael M. Mihm on 10/20/2025. Plaintiff initially filed this class action complaint in Singla v. United States, et al., C.D. Ill. Case No. 25-cv-1426, which was transferred to the Northern District of Illinois pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1404 on 10/17/2025. The action was transferred because many of the named Defendants resided in the Northern District. Singla, No. 25-cv-1426-JEH-RLH. The Court also noted that the Complaint, Motion to Proceed IFP and Motions for Expedited Discovery, Fee Waiver, Appointment of Counsel, and Other Relief identified the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division, further indicating that transfer was proper. Singla, No. 25-cv-1426-JEH-RLH. After the Court transferred his case, Plaintiff filed the present Complaint, Motion to Proceed IFP and Motions for Expedited Discovery, Fee Waiver, Appointment of Counsel, and Other Relief. These filings are substantially the same as the ones that were previously transferred, except that it names two additional defendants, and it now references the U.S. District Court for the Central District of Illinois. The Complaint even identifies the Case No. as 1:25-cv-01426-JEH-RLH. (D. 1, p. 2). Becuase this case does not significantly differ from Singla, Case No. 1:25-cv-01426-JEH-RLH, the Court finds that that dismissal is appropriate. See McReynolds v. Merrill Lynch & Co., 694 F.3d 873, 888 (7th Cir. 2012) (district court have broad discretion to dismiss a complaint "for reasons of wise judicial administration" such as, when the action is "duplicative of a parallel action already pending in another federal court") (internal citation omitted). The Clerk is directed to dismiss the complaint and all pending motions, enter judgment, and close this case. (AWR)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE CASES AND TO APPOINT INTERIM CO-LEAD COUNSEL granting (7) Motion to Consolidate Cases 1:25-cv-08479 (as Lead Case) with 1:25-cv-08555, 1:25-cv-08623; granting (7) Motion to Appoint Counsel in c ase 1:25-cv-08479-MMG. IT IS ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as set forth below: 1. The following cases are hereby consolidated: A. Adame, Rivera v. The Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-08479 (filed on October 14, 2025 by the law firm of Lynch Carpenter, LLP); B. Mingott v. The Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-08555, No. 1:25-cv-08555 (filed on October 16, 2025 by the law firms of Strauss Borrelli PLLC and Schroder, Joseph & Associates, LLP); and C. Collins v. The Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-08623 (filed on October 17, 2025 by the law firm of Shamis & Gentile, P.A.). (collectively, the "Related Actions") under the new title: "In re Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., Data Privacy Incident" pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a) (the "Consolidated Action"). 2. The Clerk of Court is DIRECTED to administratively close Mingott v. The Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-08555 and Collins v. The Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-08623. The Clerk of Court is FURTHER DIRECTED to transfer all documents already docketed in the Related Actions into the Consolidated Action. 3. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action s hall be filed under the lead case number 1:25-cv-08479, the number assigned to the first-filed case, Adame, Rivera, and shall bear the following caption: In re Institute of Culinary Education, Inc., Data Privacy Incident. 4. The case file for the Con solidated Action will be maintained under Master File No. 1:25-cv-08479. 5. All papers previously filed and served to date in the Related Actions are deemed part of the record in the Consolidated Action. 6. Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g), the Cour t hereby appoints Gerald D. Wells, III of Lynch Carpenter, LLP, Brittany Resch of Strauss Borrelli PLLC, and Leanna A. Loginov of Shamis & Gentile, P.A as Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel to act on behalf of the Plaintiffs and the class members in the Consolidated Action, with the responsibilities as further set forth. 8. Any additional plaintiffs' counsel will do all work in this litigation only at the direction of Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel. No motion, request for discovery, or other p retrial proceedings shall be initiated or filed by any Plaintiff except through Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel and no other Plaintiffs' counsel or firm shall be authorized to perform any work in the case without the express authorization of Int erim Co-Lead Class Counsel. 9. Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel shall have sole authority to communicate with Defendant's counsel and the Court on behalf of any Plaintiff unless that authority is expressly delegated to other counsel. Defendant' ;s counsel may rely on all agreements made with Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel, and such agreements shall be binding on all other Plaintiffs' counsel. 10. Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel must serve a copy of this Order and all future orders prom ptly by overnight delivery service, facsimile, or other expeditious electronic means on counsel for Plaintiffs in any related action to the extent that Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel are aware of any such action(s) and on all attorneys for Plaintiffs whose cases may subsequently be consolidated with the above actions but who have not yet registered for ECF. 11. Plaintiffs in the Consolidated Action shall file an operative Consolidated Class Action Complaint within twenty-eight (28) days of this Order. 12. This Order shall apply to any action filed in, transferred to, or removed to this Court which relates to the subject matter at issue in this case. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Margaret M. Garnett on 11/4/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-08479-MMG, 1:25-cv-08555-MMG, 1:25-cv-08623-MMG (mml)

matchedFilings.description: Sua Sponte Order Directing Transfer of Case: In their diversity-based Class Action Complaint, Plaintiffs Allison and Soofiani ("Plaintiffs") allege Defendant Air France ("Defendant") experienced a July 2025 data breach of its computer network which exposed the highly sensitive personal information of its customers, such as the Plaintiffs, to be accessible to cybercriminals, who could steal such information. (See Compl. paras. 1-4.) Plaintiffs further allege they are citizens of California and:15. Defendant, Air France, is an international company with its principal place of business in the United States located at 125 W 55th St floor 2, New York, New York 10019, USA.* * *17. This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant because Defendant maintains its principal place of business in this District and does substantial business in this District.18. Venue is proper in this District under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(2) because a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claim occurred in this District. (Compl. paras. 15, 17-18; see also Civil cover Sheet, ECF No. [1-1] (indicating "New York County" as Defendant's resident county.) Plaintiffs are mistaken that Defendant's alleged principal place of business is in this District. Businesses which maintain their principal place of business within New York City, such as Defendant, maintain their business in the Southern District of New York. See United States District Court, Southern District of New York, available at https://www.nysd.uscourts.gov/ ("The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York encompasses the counties of New York, Bronx, Westchester, Rockland, Putnam, Orange, Dutchess, and Sullivan and draws jurors from those counties. The Court hears cases in Manhattan, White Plains, and Poughkeepsie, New York." (emphasis added)).Accordingly, in its discretion and pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1404(a), the Court ORDERS the transfer of this action to the Southern District of New York "[f]or the convenience of parties and witnesses, [and] in the interest of justice." 28 U.S.C. § 1404(a); see also Corey v. United States, 11 F.4th 79, 89-90 (2d Cir. 2021) (holding it is within a court's discretion to sua sponte order the transfer of a case to another district). In making its determination, the Court has considered "inter alia: (1) the plaintiff's choice of forum, (2) the convenience of witnesses, (3) the location of relevant documents and relative ease of access to sources of proof, (4) the convenience of parties, (5) the locus of operative facts, (6) the availability of process to compel the attendance of unwilling witnesses, and (7) the relative means of the parties." D.H. Blair & Co. v. Gottdiener, 462 F.3d 95, 106-07 (2d Cir. 2006) (internal quotation marks and brackets omitted). Other than the first one, consideration of these factors weigh in favor of a transfer. See Corey, 11 F.4th at 90. Indeed, the Southern District, in which New York City is located and where Defendant is alleged to have its principal place of business, is where the operative facts occurred, and, therefore, makes it "reasonable to expect that all relevant documents, witnesses, and means of process for obtaining evidence [are] there." Id. Thus, it is reasonable to conclude the Southern District of New York is "a more convenient forum." Id. Hence, the Clerk of Court is directed to TRANSFER this case to the Southern District of New York.Ordered by Judge Joanna Seybert on 9/4/2025. c/ECF (PAK) [Transferred from New York Eastern on 9/15/2025.]

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR CONSOLIDATION AND APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL AND AN EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE granting (20) Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:25-cv-07109-AT; granting (22) Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:25-cv-07183-AT; granting (21) Letter Motion to Consolidate Cases in case 1:26-cv-00702-AT. IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 1.Butler-Adams v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. No. 1:25-cv-7109; Miamen v.Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No . 1:25-cv-7183; Godinez v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7280; Moran v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7241; Guanzon v. Louis Vuitton North America, Inc., No. 1:25-cv-7240; and Winkler v. Louis Vuitton North America , Inc., No. 1:26-cv-00702 (the "Related Cases") are consolidated pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a); 2. Consolidation of the Related Cases is appropriate because each of the actions arise from the same nucleus of operative facts. Consolid ation will eliminate duplicative discovery, prevent inconsistent pretrial rulings, and conserve the resources of the parties, their counsel and the judiciary; 3. The Related Cases are consolidated under the docket number of the first-filed Butler- Adams action, No. 1:25-cv-7109, presently before this Court and filed in this District, and any future related actions arising from the same data breach as the Related Cases which may be filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court, under th e low-numbered case with the caption In re Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. Data Breach Litigation; 4. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g), Daniel Srourian of Srourian Law Firm, P.C. and Hunter Bryson of Bryson, Harris, Suciu & De May, PLLC are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel for Plaintiffs and Israel David of Israel David LLC, Amber Schubert of Schubert Jonckheer & Kolbe LLP, Mark Reich of Levi & Korsinksky, LLP, and Steven Nathan of Hausfeld, LLP are hereb y appointed as members of an Executive Committee for Plaintiffs, with Steven Nathan serving as Chairperson of the Executive Committee; 5. All deadlines in the Related Cases are vacated; and 6. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Compla int within thirty (30) days of the Order; and 7.In accordance with the Court's January 12, 2026 Order, Defendant shall respond tothe Consolidated Class Action Complaint within forty-five (45) days after the Consolidated Class Action Complain t is filed, and the parties shall file a joint letter and proposed case management plan within sixty (60) days after the Consolidated Class Action Complaint is filed; By June 11, 2026, Plaintiffs shall file their consolidated class action complain t. The Clerk of Court is respectfully directed to consolidate these matters under the caption In re: Louis Vuitton North America, Inc. Data Breach Litigation, case number 25 Civ. 7109. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Analisa Torres on 5/12/2026) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-07109-AT et al. (vfr)

matchedFilings.description: ELECTRONIC Order transferring case to the Fort Worth Division of the Northern District of Texas. Plaintiffs filed their class action complaint in federal court against Defendants, asserting, generally, claims for violations of Title IX, false advertisement under federal and state law, breach of contract, and conspiracy. Doc. No. 1 at 14-27. None of the named Plaintiffs reside in the Dallas Division and none of the named Defendants are alleged to be Texas residents or citizens. Plaintiffs complain of Defendants' actions and/or omissions that arise (in part if not substantially) from two events that occurred in Fort Worth, Texas. See, e.g. id. at 5, 9-10, 11. A phone call with Plaintiff's counsel confirmed this and he further indicated non-opposition to the transfer of this case to the Fort Worth Division.Based on the allegations in Plaintiffs' Complaint as well as the telephone call with Plaintiffs' counsel, a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to Plaintiffs' claims occurred in Tarrant County rather than a county in the Dallas Division of the Northern District of Texas. See 28 U.S.C. § 124(a)(2). The Court finds that the case has a more substantial connection to the Fort Worth Division of the Northern District of Texas. On the Court's own motion, this case is TRANSFERRED to the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas, Fort Worth Division. See 28 U.S.C. § 1404(a).(Ordered by Judge Ed Kinkeade on 8/27/2025) (chmb)

matchedFilings.description: Minute Entry for proceedings held before Judge P. Kevin Castel: Case Management Conference held on 12/3/2025. Appearing for plaintiffs, Charles E. Schaffer, Ashley Crooks, John Yanchunis, William Federman, Rachele Byrd, Gerald Wells, III, Amber Schubert, and Gregory Haroutunian. Appearing for defendant, James Pastore. Plaintiffs to file a proposed Order on the appointment of interim co-lead counsel no later than December 10, 2025. Consolidated class action complaint to be filed by January 26, 2026. Defendants to answer or file a pre-motion letter by February 27, 2026. Plaintiffs to respond by March 6, 2026. (Court Reporter Martha Martin) (Nacanther, Florence)

ORDER CONSOLIDATING RELATED ACTIONS AND APPOINTING INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL: Therefore, FOR GOOD CAUSE SHOWN, the Court enters the following ORDER: 1. The following Related Actions are hereby consolidated pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a): (1) Quintero, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-05541-PKC, filed on July 3, 2025; (2) Holmes v. Trustees ofColwnbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06232- PKC, filed on July 29, 2025; (3) Murray v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06283- PKC, filed on July 30, 2025; (4) McQueen v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06622- PKC, filed on August 11, 2025; (5) Daley v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06665- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (6) Hall v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06664- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (7) Sabedra v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv- 06698-PKC, filed on August 13, 2025; (8) Nadeau v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06720-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; (9) Babb v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06745-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; and (10) Linich, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06928-PKC, filed on August 21, 2025 (collectively, the "Consolidated Action"). 2. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action shall be filed under Case No. 1:25-cv- 05541-PKC, the number assigned to the lowest-numbered case, and shall bear the following caption: As further set forth by this Order. 6. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g)(3), Charles Schaffer of Levin Sedran & Berman LLP, William B. Fedennan ofFedennan & Sherwood, Rachele R. Byrd of Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP, and Ashley Crooks of Hausfeld LLP are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel. Co-Lead Class Counsel are designated to "act on behalf of a putative class before determining whether to certify the action as a class action" and are responsible for coordinating pretrial proceedings. Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g)(3). Co-Lead Class Counsel's responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: As further set forth by this Order. 8. The Court sets the following case schedule: a. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint by January 26, 2026. b. Defendants shall answer or file a pre-motion letter by February 27, 2026. c. Plaintiffs shall to respond to any pre-motion letter by March 6, 2026. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge P. Kevin Castel on 12/11/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-05541-PKC et al. (tg) (Entered: 12/11/2025)

Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Gelbspan et al (25 CV 10397) - Blake Yagman, Esq. appears telephonically. (25 CV 10633) - Candice Enders, Esq. is present. Counsel for Plaintiff(s) Lee et al (26 CV 329) - Christopher Micheletti, Esq. is present. Counsel(s) for Defendant(s) PepsiCo, Inc. and PepsiCo Beverage Sales, LLC, Jay Srinivasan, Esq. and Laura O'Boyle, Esq., are present. Counsel for Defendant Walmart, Inc., Lawrence Buterman, Esq., is present. Law Clerk Ryan Miller is present. Plaintiffs' brief(s) (joint or contested) regarding leadership for direct purchaser Plaintiffs to be submitted by March 6, 2026. Reply briefs, if any, to be submitted by March 13, 2026. matchedFilings.description: Minute Entry for proceedings held before Judge P. Kevin Castel: Case Management Conference held on 12/3/2025. Appearing for plaintiffs, Charles E. Schaffer, Ashley Crooks, John Yanchunis, William Federman, Rachele Byrd, Gerald Wells, III, Amber Schubert, and Gregory Haroutunian. Appearing for defendant, James Pastore. Plaintiffs to file a proposed Order on the appointment of interim co-lead counsel no later than December 10, 2025. Consolidated class action complaint to be filed by January 26, 2026. Defendants to answer or file a pre-motion letter by February 27, 2026. Plaintiffs to respond by March 6, 2026. (Court Reporter Martha Martin) (Nacanther, Florence)

ORDER CONSOLIDATING RELATED ACTIONS AND APPOINTING INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL: Therefore, FOR GOOD CAUSE SHOWN, the Court enters the following ORDER: 1. The following Related Actions are hereby consolidated pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a): (1) Quintero, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-05541-PKC, filed on July 3, 2025; (2) Holmes v. Trustees ofColwnbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06232- PKC, filed on July 29, 2025; (3) Murray v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06283- PKC, filed on July 30, 2025; (4) McQueen v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06622- PKC, filed on August 11, 2025; (5) Daley v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06665- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (6) Hall v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06664- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (7) Sabedra v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv- 06698-PKC, filed on August 13, 2025; (8) Nadeau v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06720-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; (9) Babb v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06745-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; and (10) Linich, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06928-PKC, filed on August 21, 2025 (collectively, the "Consolidated Action"). 2. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action shall be filed under Case No. 1:25-cv- 05541-PKC, the number assigned to the lowest-numbered case, and shall bear the following caption: As further set forth by this Order. 6. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g)(3), Charles Schaffer of Levin Sedran & Berman LLP, William B. Fedennan ofFedennan & Sherwood, Rachele R. Byrd of Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP, and Ashley Crooks of Hausfeld LLP are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel. Co-Lead Class Counsel are designated to "act on behalf of a putative class before determining whether to certify the action as a class action" and are responsible for coordinating pretrial proceedings. Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g)(3). Co-Lead Class Counsel's responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: As further set forth by this Order. 8. The Court sets the following case schedule: a. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint by January 26, 2026. b. Defendants shall answer or file a pre-motion letter by February 27, 2026. c. Plaintiffs shall to respond to any pre-motion letter by March 6, 2026. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge P. Kevin Castel on 12/11/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-05541-PKC et al. (tg) (Entered: 12/11/2025)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a), the Court may consolidate actions that involve common question of law or facts. The matter is before the Court on the unopposed motion to consolidate related actions and appoint interim lead counsel. (Doc. No. 26). The motion to consolidate is GRANTED and the motion to appoint interim lead counsel is RESERVED. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action shall be filed under the lead case number 3:25-cv-00755, the number assigned to the first-filed case, and shall bear the following caption. All future pleadings shall be filed in the lead case only. The Clerk shall administratively close the following cases: 3:25-cv-776, 3:25-cv-798, 3:25-cv-799, 3:25-cv-819, 3:25-cv-832, 3:25-cv-852. With consideration, Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaint on or before December 15, 2025. Defendants shall answer or otherwise respond on or before January 20, 2025. After the Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaint is filed, Plaintiffs may renew the motion to appoint interim class action counsel. Signed by District Judge Waverly D. Crenshaw, Jr on 11/07/2025. (DOCKET TEXT SUMMARY ONLY-ATTORNEYS MUST OPEN THE PDF AND READ THE ORDER.)(ad) (Entered: 11/10/2025)

July 5, 2022), having found that these actions involve common questions of law and fact, and recognizin g that the parties and counsel have previously indicated to the court their consent to consolidation of these matters, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT:1.The stay previously entered in the above-captioned actions is hereby LIFTED;2.Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a)(2), the above-captioned actions are CONSOLIDATED for all purposes;3.The clerk is directed to consolidate the case docketed as Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01290 into the case docketed as Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01057;4.The clerk is directed to CLOSE the case docketed as Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01290;5.The clerk is directed to enter on the docket of the consolidated case, Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01057, the appearances of all counsel of record previously entered on behalf of plaintiff Bren den Smith in the discontinued case, Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01290;6.All future documents filed in this consolidated case shall be filed under Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01057; and7.The defendants shall file their answer or other response to the Consolidated Class Action Complaint (Doc. 26) within thirty (30) days after entry of this order. Signed by Honorable Joseph F. Saporito, Jr on 6/25/26. (ms)

ORDER CONSOLIDATING RELATED ACTIONS AND APPOINTING INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL: Therefore, FOR GOOD CAUSE SHOWN, the Court enters the following ORDER: 1. The following Related Actions are hereby consolidated pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a): (1) Quintero, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-05541-PKC, filed on July 3, 2025; (2) Holmes v. Trustees ofColwnbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06232- PKC, filed on July 29, 2025; (3) Murray v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06283- PKC, filed on July 30, 2025; (4) McQueen v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06622- PKC, filed on August 11, 2025; (5) Daley v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06665- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (6) Hall v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06664- PKC, filed on August 12, 2025; (7) Sabedra v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv- 06698-PKC, filed on August 13, 2025; (8) Nadeau v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06720-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; (9) Babb v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25- cv-06745-PKC, filed on August 14, 2025; and (10) Linich, et al. v. Trustees of Columbia University, No. 1:25-cv-06928-PKC, filed on August 21, 2025 (collectively, the "Consolidated Action"). 2. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action shall be filed under Case No. 1:25-cv- 05541-PKC, the number assigned to the lowest-numbered case, and shall bear the following caption: As further set forth by this Order. 6. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(g)(3), Charles Schaffer of Levin Sedran & Berman LLP, William B. Fedennan ofFedennan & Sherwood, Rachele R. Byrd of Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP, and Ashley Crooks of Hausfeld LLP are hereby appointed Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel. Co-Lead Class Counsel are designated to "act on behalf of a putative class before determining whether to certify the action as a class action" and are responsible for coordinating pretrial proceedings. Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g)(3). Co-Lead Class Counsel's responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: As further set forth by this Order. 8. The Court sets the following case schedule: a. Plaintiffs shall file a Consolidated Class Action Complaint by January 26, 2026. b. Defendants shall answer or file a pre-motion letter by February 27, 2026. c. Plaintiffs shall to respond to any pre-motion letter by March 6, 2026. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge P. Kevin Castel on 12/11/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-05541-PKC et al. (tg) (Entered: 12/11/2025)

matchedFilings.description: ENDORSED ORDER denying Defendant's motion (Dkt. 22) to dismiss Plaintiffs' amended class action complaint (Dkt. 16) under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(b)(6) for the reasons stated in Plaintiffs' response (Dkt. 23) to the motion. Namely, Plaintiffs plausibly plead that Defendant disclosed their confidential medical information to third parties, did so without Plaintiffs' authorization for advertising purposes through tracking technologies related to Defendant's website, and thereby violated the Florida Security of Communications Act (FSCA) and the Electronic Communications Privacy Act (ECPA), breached Plaintiffs' confidence, and was unjustly enriched. (See Dkt. 16.) See W.W. v. Orlando Health, Inc., No. 6:24-cv-1068-JSS-RMN, 2025 WL 722892, 2025 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 40038 (M.D. Fla. Mar. 6, 2025) (declining to dismiss FSCA, ECPA, breach of confidence, and unjust enrichment claims in a highly similar case when a defendant healthcare organization allegedly disclosed its patients' confidential medical information to third parties and did so without the patients' authorization for advertising purposes through tracking technologies related to the defendant's website); see also Lopez v. Win, No. 6:10-cv-1887-ORL-35KRS, 2011 WL 13174851, at *2, 2011 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 166372, at *5 (M.D. Fla. Mar. 18, 2011) ("The threshold for surviving a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim under [Federal Rule of Civil Procedure] 12(b)(6) is a low one."), aff'd sub nom. Lopez v. Target Corp., 676 F.3d 1230 (11th Cir. 2012). Accordingly, Defendant's motion (Dkt. 22) is DENIED. Signed by Judge Julie S. Sneed on 3/12/2026. (AJL) (Entered: 03/12/2026)

Upon consideration of the motio n, any responses or oppositions thereto from counsel for Defendant and counsel for Plaintiffs in the related cases, and all supporting papers filed in support of the motion or any response or opposition thereto, FOR GOOD CAUSE SHOWN, Plaintiff's motion is HEREBY GRANTED. The following actions are hereby consolidated pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a): (1) Thompson v. Apex Global Solutions, LLC, No. 7:25-cv-05021; (2) Morrison v. Apex Global Solutions LLC, No. 1:25-cv-05034; ( 3) Williams v. Apex Global Solutions, LLC, No. 7:25-cv-05040; and (4) Daly v. Apex Global Solutions, LLC, No. 1:25-cv-05198 (collectively, the "Consolidated Actions"). matchedFilings.description: TEXT ORDER: Defendant Communications Data Group, Inc.'s ("CDG") 21 Unopposed Fourth Motion for Extension of Time to Answer or Otherwise Plead is GRANTED. Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b)(1)(A), the Court may, for good cause, extend the time when a request is made before the original deadline expires. Here, the Court consolidated several pending cases on August 5, 2025. On September 18, 2025, the Court granted Plaintiffs' motion to appoint interim class counsel and set new deadlines for (1) Plaintiffs to file a consolidated class action complaint and (2) CDG to respond to that complaint. (See Doc. 19.) Given these circumstances, the Court finds good cause to extend CDG's time to respond to the individual complaints. Accordingly, CDG's deadline to respond to the Pierce and Watson complaints is extended to November 10, 2025. Entered by Magistrate Judge Ronald L. Hanna on October 14, 2025. (NL)

AMENDED COMPLAINT Consolidated Class Action Complaint against Communications Data Group Inc, Communications Data Group Inc, Cumberland Cellular LLC, Duo County Telephone Cooperative Corporation Inc, filed by Michele Watson, Rilda Firkins, Shannon Pierce, Patty Bennett.(Klinger, Gary) (Entered: 10/20/2025)

TEXT ORDER: The parties have filed a 25 joint motion to stay the case. In it, they explain that they have agreed to mediate the dispute, that the mediation is set to take place in January 2026, and that a stay would avoid potentially unnecessary litigation. The Court finds this approach sensible. Accordingly, the parties' 25 motion is GRANTED and this case is STAYED. See Landis v. North American Co., 299 U.S. 248, 254 (1936) (explaining that district court has inherent power to stay proceedings). The parties are further ORDERED to file a status report within fourteen days of the conclusion of the mediation. Finally, the Court adopts the parties' suggestion that their post-mediation status report set forth proposed deadlines for the defendants responses to the plaintiffs' 22 consolidated class action complaint and a briefing schedule, if necessary. Entered by Magistrate Judge Ronald L. Hanna on November 20, 2025. (NL)

matchedFilings.description: NOTICE re 1 Complaint, Extension of Time to Respond to Plaintiffs' Putative Class Action Complaint by Defendant Nestle Purina Pet Care Co. (Rosenwasser, Steven) Modified on 7/8/2025 to add a gavel per chambers (tlove, ). (Entered: 07/02/2025)

MINUTE ORDER: Before the Court is the defendant's Notice of Extension of Time to Respond to Plaintiffs' Putative Class Action Complaint. ECF No. 10 . The defendant, pursuant to D.C.COLO.LCivR 6.1(a), seeks an additional twenty-eight days to file its response to the Complaint. D.C.COLO.LCivR 6.1(a), however, only allows for parties to stipulate to an extension of no more than twenty-one days, and "[a]ny other request for an extension of time or continuance must be approved by court order on motion." As the defendant seeks an extension of time beyond what the rule allows, the defendant was required to file a motion. See id.; see also D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.1(c). However, in the interest of judicial efficiency, the Court construes the defendant's filing as a motion. For good cause shown, the Motion, ECF No. 10, is GRANTED. Accordingly, the defendant shall file its response to the plaintiffs' complaint on or before August 1, 2025. Entered by Magistrate Judge Cyrus Y. Chung on 7/8/2025. (tlove, ) (Entered: 07/08/2025)

matchedFilings.description: TEXT ORDER: Plaintiff Richard Hussey, individually and on behalf of all others similarly situated in the United States, has brought a class action complaint against Bradford Health Services LLC. (Doc. 1 ). Mr. Hussey alleges that the Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d). (Doc. 1, p. 6, 25). Section 1332(d) provides that "district courts shall have original jurisdiction of any civil action in which the matter in controversy exceeds the sum or value of $5,000,000, exclusive of interest and costs, and is a class action in which... any member of a class of plaintiffs is a citizen of a State different from any defendant." § 1332(d)(2)(A). Mr. Hussey alleges that the "amount in controversy in this Class action exceeds $5,000,000, exclusive of interest and costs, and there are numerous Class members who are citizens of states other than Defendants state of citizenship." (Doc. 1, p. 6, 25). For individuals, citizenship rests on the concept of domicile. Smith v. Marcus & Millichap, Inc., 991 F.3d 1145, 1149 (11th Cir. 2021) (citation omitted). Domicile "consists of two elements: residency in a state and intent to remain in that state." Smith, 991 F.3d at 1149 (citation omitted). "Residency is necessary, but insufficient, to establish citizenship in a state. Smith, 991 F.3d at 1149 (citation omitted). "[A] limited liability company is a citizen of any state of which a member of the company is a citizen." Flintlock Constr. Servs., LLC v. Well-Come Holdings, LLC, 710 F.3d 1221, 1224 (11th Cir. 2013) (internal quotation marks and quotation omitted). Based on these citizenship standards, Mr. Hussey has not alleged subject matter jurisdiction for this matter sufficiently. Mr. Hussey states that he is a resident of Alabama, but he does not allege his citizenship. (See Doc. 1, p. 5, 19). Mr. Hussey has identified Bradford's principal place of business, but Mr. Hussey has not alleged the citizenship of Bradford's members. (See Doc. 1, p. 6, 23). Because Mr. Hussey has not properly alleged Bradfords citizenship and his citizenship or a diverse class member's citizenship, the Court cannot ascertain whether this action meets the minimal diversity requirement of § 1332(d). The threshold is low, but Mr. Hussey must provide more information to allow the Court to confirm subject matter jurisdiction. 28 U.S.C. § 1653 allows a party to amend defective allegations of jurisdiction. § 1653. Accordingly, on or before June 18, 2025, Mr. Hussey shall please amend his complaint to clarify his citizenship allegations. Signed by Judge Madeline Hughes Haikala on 06/05/2025. (CLD) (Entered: 06/05/2025)

(Attachments: # 1 Exhibit Exhibit 1 to Complaint_Subpoena and Parking Pass, # 2 Exhibit Exhibit 2 to Complaint_Stewart Gollan Declaration) (Johnson, R.) (Entered: 05/05/2025)

DOCKET TEXT ORDER. Having carefully reviewed 12 Ex Parte Motion for Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction, the court finds that Plaintiff has failed to justify an ex parte temporary restraining order under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 65(b)(1). As the Supreme Court has explained, the issuance of ex parte temporary restraining orders is subject to "stringent restrictions" because "our entire jurisprudence runs counter to the notion of court action taken before reasonable notice and an opportunity to be heard has been granted both sides of a dispute." Granny Goose Foods, Inc. v. Teamsters, 415 U.S. 423, 438–39 (1974). To the extent Plaintiff seeks an ex parte temporary restraining order, her motion is accordingly DENIED. (Her motion otherwise remains pending.)Plaintiff shall promptly serve Defendants with a copy of 1 Class Action Complaint, a copy of 12 Ex Parte Motion for Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction and the supporting declaration and exhibits, as well as a copy of this docket text order. Once Plaintiff has served these documents on Defendants, she shall promptly file proof of service. Defendants shall file a response to 12 Ex Parte Motion for Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction no later than seven days after receipt of service. Plaintiff may file a reply no later than three days after Defendants file a response. If any of these deadlines falls on a weekend or a federal holiday, the response or reply may be filed by the end of the next business day. SO ORDERED. Signed by Judge Howard C. Nielson, Jr., on 5/9/2025. No attached document. (jse) (Entered: 05/09/2025)

matchedFilings.description: MINUTE entry before the Honorable Joan B. Gottschall: Plaintiff commenced this civil action by filing a 100-page class action complaint 1 under § 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 1 et seq., and the Commodity Exchange Act, 7 U.S.C. §§ 9 et seq., on April 24, 2025. Within three weeks and before any defendant appeared, plaintiff filed a notice 22 purporting to dismiss the case voluntarily without prejudice under Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a)(1)(A)(i).The rule permitting a plaintiff to dismiss an action voluntarily without a court order is "Subject to Rules 23(e)," among other rules. Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a). Rule 23(e) provides: "The claims, issues, or defenses of a certified class-or a class proposed to be certified for purposes of settlement-may be settled, voluntarily dismissed, or compromised only with the court's approval," and specifies sending notice and holding a fairness hearing. The Seventh Circuit has held that Rule 23(e), must be observed not only where the court has certified a class but also where a plaintiff settles or voluntarily dismisses a "putative [class], that is, the class alleged in the complaint." Culver v. City of Milwaukee, 277 F.3d 908, 914 (7th Cir. 2002) (citations omitted); See In re AT&T Mobility Wireless Data Servs. Sales Litig., 270 F.R.D. 330, 351 (N.D. Ill. 2010). However, "if it is plain that there is no prejudice, violation of the rule is harmless and compliance will not be ordered." Culver, 277 F.3d at 915 (citations omitted). In view of these authorities, plaintiff is instructed to file a brief memorandum of law on or before May 21, 2025, making clear for the record, if it is indeed the case, that there is no prejudice to the class.Mailed notice (mjc, ) (Entered: 05/15/2025)

matchedFilings.description: ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS' MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE ACTIONS AND APPOINT INTERIM CO-LEAD CLASS COUNSEL AND SCHEDULING ORDER granting (19) Motion to Consolidate Cases; granting (19) Motion to Appoint Counsel in case 1:25-cv-03374-GHW-KHP. IT IS HE REBY ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED as follows: 1. Julianne Cook v. Legends International, LLC, Case No. 1:25-cv-03374 (S.D.N.Y); Domonique Barlow v. Legends International, LLC, No. 1:25-cv-03835 (S.D.N.Y.); Katherine Heldreth v. Legends International, LLC, No. 1:25-cv-04073 (S.D.N.Y.); and all other actions (now and in the future) naming Legends International, LLC, as a defendant in connection with the Data Breach that occurred in November 2024 shall be conso lidated pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42 under case number of the first-filed case 1:25-cv-03374 (the "Consolidated Action"). 2. All papers filed in the Consolidated Acon shall be filed under Case No. No.1:25- cv-03374 an d shall bear the following capon: In re Legends International, LLC, Data Breach Litigation. Any action subsequently filed, transferred, or removed to The Court that arises out of the same or similar operative facts as the Consolidated Action will b e consolidated with it for pretrial, discovery, and trial purposes. 3. The Court hereby appoints Britany Resch of Strauss Borrelli PLLC, Jeff Ostrow of Kopelowitz Ostrow P.A., and William B. Federman of Federman & Sherwood as Interim Co-Lead Couns el to act on behalf of the Plaintiffs and the putative Class with the following responsibilities and sole authority to, as further set forth herein. 4. Unless otherwise ordered by the Court upon a showing of good cause, this Order shall apply to the above-referenced maters, any action filed in, transferred to, or removed to The Court which relates to the subject mater at issue in this case. 5. Plaintiffs in the Consolidated Action shall file an operative, Consolidated Class Action Compla int within 45 days of this Order. Defendant need not respond to any of the previously filed complaints in the Related Actions and will respond to the operative Consolidated Class Action Complaint within 60 days after it is filed. If Defendant' s response is a motion to dismiss, filed according to the Court's procedures, Plaintiffs shall have 30 days to respond thereto, and Defendant 30 days to file a reply.6.The Initial Case Management Conferences scheduled for July 24, 2025 in 25-cv- 3835 and for August 11, 2025 in 25-cv-4073 are adjourned. Instead, an initial case management conference in this Consolidated Action shall be held on September 25, 2025 at 10:00 a.m. in Courtroom 17D. IT IS SO ORDERED. (Signed by Magistrate Judge Katharine H. Parker on 6/18/2025) Filed In Associated Cases: 1:25-cv-03374-GHW-KHP, 1:25-cv-03835-GHW-KHP, 1:25-cv-04073-GHW-KHP (vfr)

R. Civ. P. 42(a), and shall be consolidated into the docket of the first-filed Ding action, No. 1:25-cv-02416. (2) The clerk shall administratively terminate all other Related Actions. The case file for the Consolidated Action will be maintained under Master File No. 1:25-cv-02416 (i.e., Ding). (3) Any action subsequently filed in, transferred to, or removed to this Court that arises out of the same or similar operative facts as the Consolidated Action shall be consolidated with the Consolidated Action for pre-trial purposes. The parties shall file a Notice of Related Action whenever a case that should be consolidated into this action is filed in, transferred to, or removed to this District. (6) A Consolidated Class Action Complaint shall be filed within 45 days following the date of the Courts order appointing interim class counsel. Defendant need not respond to any of the individual complaints filed in any of the Related Actions. Following appointment of interim class counsel, the parties shall confer and submit for the Court's consideration an agreed-upon briefing schedule for any motion to dismiss briefing. SO STIPULATED BY THE PARTIES. (And as further set forth herein.) SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Edgardo Ramos on 6/20/2025) (jca) (Entered: 06/20/2025)

R. Civ. P. 42(a), and shall be consolidated into the docket of the first-filed Ding action, No. 1:25-cv-02416. (2) The clerk shall administratively terminate all other Related Actions. The case file for the Consolidated Action will be maintained under Master File No. 1:25-cv-02416 (i.e., Ding). (3) Any action subsequently filed in, transferred to, or removed to this Court that arises out of the same or similar operative facts as the Consolidated Action shall be consolidated with the Consolidated Action for pre-trial purposes. The parties shall file a Notice of Related Action whenever a case that should be consolidated into this action is filed in, transferred to, or removed to this District. (6) A Consolidated Class Action Complaint shall be filed within 45 days following the date of the Courts order appointing interim class counsel. Defendant need not respond to any of the individual complaints filed in any of the Related Actions. Following appointment of interim class counsel, the parties shall confer and submit for the Court's consideration an agreed-upon briefing schedule for any motion to dismiss briefing. matchedFilings.description: STIPULATION AND ORDER TO CONSOLIDATE RELATED ACTIONS AND SET BRIEFING SCHEDULE FOR INTERIM CLASS COUNSEL APPLICATIONS: NOW THEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, all the parties in the Related Actions AGREE AND STIPULATE as follows: (1) The Related Actions are appropriate for consolidation under Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a), and shall be consolidated into the docket of the first-filed Ding action, No. 1:25-cv-02416. (2) The clerk shall administratively terminate all other Related Actions. The case file for the Consolidated Action will be maintained under Master File No. 1:25-cv-02416 (i.e., Ding). (3) Any action subsequently filed in, transferred to, or removed to this Court that arises out of the same or similar operative facts as the Consolidated Action shall be consolidated with the Consolidated Action for pre-trial purposes. The parties shall file a Notice of Related Action whenever a case that should be consolidated into this action is filed in, transferred to, or removed to this District. (6) A Consolidated Class Action Complaint shall be filed within 45 days following the date of the Courts order appointing interim class counsel. Defendant need not respond to any of the individual complaints filed in any of the Related Actions. Following appointment of interim class counsel, the parties shall confer and submit for the Court's consideration an agreed-upon briefing schedule for any motion to dismiss briefing. SO STIPULATED BY THE PARTIES. (And as further set forth herein.) SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Edgardo Ramos on 6/20/2025) (jca) (Entered: 06/20/2025)

R. Civ. P. 42(a), and shall be consolidated into the docket of the first-filed Ding action, No. 1:25-cv-02416. (2) The clerk shall administratively terminate all other Related Actions. The case file for the Consolidated Action will be maintained under Master File No. 1:25-cv-02416 (i.e., Ding). (6) A Consolidated Class Action Complaint shall be filed within 45 days following the date of the Courts order appointing interim class counsel. Defendant need not respond to any of the individual complaints filed in any of the Related Actions. Following appointment of interim class counsel, the parties shall confer and submit for the Court's consideration an agreed-upon briefing schedule for any motion to dismiss briefing. SO STIPULATED BY THE PARTIES. (And as further set forth herein.) SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Edgardo Ramos on 6/20/2025) (jca) (Entered: 06/20/2025)

PAPERLESS ORDER granting 36 Joint Motion to Stay Discovery and Discovery-Based Deadlines Pending Resolution of Defendant's Motion to Dismiss ("Joint Motion"). District courts enjoy broad discretion in deciding how to best manage the cases before them. See Johnson v. Bd. of Regents of Univ. of Ga., 263 F.3d 1234, 1269 (11th Cir. 2001); see also Chrysler Int'l Corp. v. Chemaly, 280 F.3d 1358, 1360 (11th Cir. 2002). And "[a] stay of discovery is appropriate where the movant shows good cause and reasonableness." Varga v. Palm Beach Cap. Mgmt., LLC, No. 09-82398, 2010 WL 8510622, at *1 (S.D. Fla. Sept. 3, 2010) (citation and internal quotation marks omitted); see also Point Conversions, LLC v. Lopane, No. 20-61549, 2020 WL 6700236, at *2 (S.D. Fla. Oct. 29, 2020) (staying discovery pending a decision on defendant's motion to dismiss which "raise[s] serious questions regarding the viability of Plaintiff's Complaint that must be resolved before Defendant is burdened with discovery and other pretrial obligations"). Further, where a pending motion may dispose of the entire action, granting a stay of discovery may be justified. See Chudasama v. Mazda Motor Corp., 123 F. 3d 1353, 1367 (11th Cir. 1997) ("Facial challenges to the legal sufficiency of a claim or defense, such as a motion to dismiss based on failure to state a claim for relief, should... be resolved before discovery begins." (footnote omitted)); see also Goldstein v. Costco Wholesale Corp., No. 21-80601, 2021 WL 2827757, at *2 (S.D. Fla. July 8, 2021) ("When faced with legitimate challenges to the legal theory upon which a broad class action complaint rests, a temporary stay of discovery is the proper course until such challenges are resolved.").Here, a stay of discovery is warranted. Defendant Publix Super Markets, Inc. has filed a Motion to Dismiss, ECF No. 29, which is currently under advisement. Defendant argues that Plaintiff lacks standing and fails to state any viable causes of action. See generally Mot. to Dismiss. Because some of the arguments, including lack of standing, could result in the dismissal of the action - or at the very least dismissal of certain claims - a stay of discovery is warranted pending resolution of the Motion. Accordingly, the parties' Joint Motion is GRANTED. The Court will determine if discovery in this action should proceed following adjudication of the pending Motion to Dismiss, at which point the Court, if necessary, will also set a status conference to address the need for a revised scheduling order. Further, although the Court is staying discovery and discovery-based deadlines in this matter, the parties shall proceed with their scheduled mediation, see ECF No. 28, and are strongly encouraged to explore the possibility of scheduling earlier mediation by agreement, as contemplated in the parties' Joint Motion. See Joint Motion at 3. Signed by Judge Rodolfo A. Ruiz, II on 9/24/2025. (mb03) (Entered: 09/24/2025)

matchedFilings.description: TEXT ORDER: The Court has reviewed Plaintiffs' motion for leave to file an Amended Class and Collective Action Complaint substituting Opt-In Plaintiff Rysell Ruan as the named plaintiff and to stay the claims of Lead Plaintiff David Pineda and Opt-In Plaintiffs Venassa Rincon Ubri and Jose Ruan in this matter pending the resolution of arbitration, pursuant to 9 U.S.C. § 3. ECF No. 26 . The Court notes that Plaintiffs do not address whether the Court will continue to have jurisdiction over this matter should it grant Plaintiffs' request for Lead Plaintiff Pineda's claim to be stayed pending his individual arbitration. As courts in this District have noted, important here, "a named plaintiff's ability to amend a complaint and name a new putative class representative depends on the named plaintiff's claim remaining justiciable." Gaddy v. Long & Foster Companies, Inc., No. CV 21-2396 (RBK)(EAP), 2023 WL 1926654, at *5 (D.N.J. Feb. 10, 2023)(citing Lusardi v. Xerox Corp., 975 F.2d 964, 974 (3d Cir. 1992)). Indeed, "Article III standing demands that a plaintiff's claim remain live throughout the entire litigation." Id. (citing Lusardi, 975 F.2d at 974). Due to the Court's questions as to standing, Plaintiffs' motion at ECF No. 26 is DENIED WITHOUT PREJUDICE. Any renewed motion to amend must include sufficient facts and legal authority supporting this Court's continued jurisdiction under Article III should Lead Plaintiff Pineda be substituted. So Ordered by Magistrate Judge Jose R. Almonte on 9/25/2025. (akw, ) (Entered: 09/25/2025)
